class tiarsdesigner.Designer(sequence, cutsite, Renzyme_list=None)[source]¶

The parent class for Endogenous and Candidate, which stores functions and variables common to both

Parameters¶

sequence: string

An in frame sequence of DNA nucleotides of max length 273 nucleotides. It should have a PAM sequence that makes it suitable for CRISPR/Cas9 activity.

cutsite: int

The index location of the CRISPR/Cas9 cutsite (3 nt after the PAM if it’s CCN, 3 before if it’s NGG).

Renzyme_list: list

Optional: provide a list of Renzymes to use. Default is Bio.Restriction AllEnzymes.

Attributes:¶

sequence: string

The input sequence.

cutsite: int

The input cutsite

cutsite_region: string

a subset of sequence that extends 15 bp to either side of cutsite.

cutsite_frame: int

a number describing the frame of the cutsite region. ‘0’ means it’s in frame. ‘1’ means the second bp of the cutsite region is the first bp of the first codon, and ‘2’ means the third bp of the cutsite region is the first bp of the first codon.

Renzymes: dict

a dictionary of restriction enzymes with a recognition sites in self.sequence, with re names as keys and their cutsite as the values.

splicing_hexamers: dict

a dictionary of splicing hexamers found in self.sequence with the hexamer sequences as keys and their locations in self.sequence as values. splicing hexamers, aka exonic splicing enhancers, are 6 nt sequences that enhance premrna splicing. the list of possible hexamers comes from rescue-ese (http://genes.mit.edu/burgelab/rescue-ese/). This dictionary will help us filter out candidates that interfere with splicing by modifying any of the splicing enhancers

get_distance_from(pos=0)[source]¶

Takes all of the restriction enzymes in self.Renzymes and returns a dictionary with REnames as their values and their distances from pos as the values.

Parameters¶

pos: int

an integer in range(0, len(self.sequence))

Returns¶

A dictionary of Restriction enzymes that would cut the sequence, with the enzymes as keys and the distances between their cutsites and pos as values. A positive distance means that the REcutsite is later in the string than pos, while a negative distance means that the REcutsite appears before pos in the string.

get_splicing_hexamers(sequence)[source]¶

This function searches the input sequence for splicing hexamers (6 nt sequences that enhance premRNA splicing, AKA exonic splicing enhancers) from the list provided by RESCUE-ESE (http://genes.mit.edu/burgelab/rescue-ese/zebrafish). This list has been copied into ‘splicing_hexamers.txt’ with duplicate hexamers removed and returns a dictionary of splicing hexamers found in the input sequence and their locations in the sequence.

Parameters¶

sequence: string

A DNA nucleotide sequence. Must be all capital letters.

Returns¶

Dictionary of hexamers in the sequence with the hexamer sequences as keys and their locations in the input sequence as values

class tiarsdesigner.Endogenous(sequence, gRNA_start, gRNA_end, PAM_start, which_PAM, AA_change_site, new_codon, Renzyme_list=None)[source]¶

Bases: Designer

An Endogenous object is a subclass of the designer class, and an Endogenous object is the endogenous sequence for a CRISPR/Cas9 experiment before any edits are made to the sequence

Parameters¶

sequence: string

The endogenous/wt dna sequence without any synonymous changes and without the desired CRISPR facilitated amino acid change. Max length is 273 bp, must be in frame.

gRNA_start: int

the index location in the sequence of the beginning of the region the CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA will target.

gRNA_end: int

the index location in the sequence of the end of the region the CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA will target.

PAM_start: int

The index location in the sequence of the beginning of the PAM site. For now, the PAM region has to be either ‘CCN’ or ‘NGG’.

which_PAM: string

The sequence of the PAM site (e.g. ‘NGG’ or ‘CCN’ for Cas9, or ‘TTTN’ or ‘BAAA’ for Cfp1)

AA_change_site: int

the index location in the sequence of the beginning of the codon that is to be nonsynonymously changed in the CRISPR/Cas9 process

new_codon: string

the codon to replace the existing codon at the AA_change_site

Attributes¶

From Parent Class:

sequence cutsite (determined based on the PAM location and whether it’s ‘CCN’ or ‘NGG’) cutsite_region cutsite_frame Renzymes splicing_hexamers

Unique to Endogenous Class:

gRNA_location: tuple

A tuple of the start and end coordinates of the region in sequence to be targeted by the guide RNA.

PAM_start: int

The index location of the beginning of the PAM site in sequence. For now, the PAM site has to be either ‘CCN’ or ‘NGG’.

cas9_cut_from_PAM: int

The location of the CRISPR/Cas9 cutsite in the sequence relative to the PAM_start site. For ‘CCN’ it will be 6, and for ‘NGG’ it will be -3. Since the value is different for each PAM, it is also useful for indicating whether the PAM sequence is ‘CCN’ or ‘NGG’.

AA_change_site: int

The index location in the sequence of the codon that is to be nonsynonymously changed in the CRISPR/Cas9 process.

AA_change_sequence:

A sequence identical to the endogenous sequence (self.sequence), but it has the new_codon substitution at the AA site. In other words, it’s the endogenous sequence with the desired CRISPR/Cas9 nonsynonymous substitution.

PAM_can_change: bool

a boolean value indicating whether or not the PAM site can be interrupted via only synonymous substitutions. This means that one or both of the non ‘N’ basepair’s in the PAM site can be changed to anything else without changing the resulting amino acid sequence. This value will also be True if the desired amino acid change interrupts the PAM.

get_filtered_candidates(locusname, single_enzyme_filters, min_Rsite_distance, get_filter_stats, codon_usage_tsv)[source]¶

Builds a generator of all potential repair oligo candidates with the desired nonsynonymous amino acid change and at least one synonymous substitution in self.cutsite_region. Before being run through the generator, however, each candidate-Renzyme combination is run through all of the single Renzyme filters, and only the combinations that pass all of them go through.

Parameters¶

locusname: string

A user created name for the locus for writing the filter stats to file

single_enzyme_filters: list

A list of filters to run for this locus (will run all filters if not specified)

min_Rsite_distance: int

An integer indicating the minimum allowable distance between any novel and endogenous site for a given restriction enzyme

get_filter_stats: bool

A boolean value indicating whether or not the function should generate filter stats in the form of a percentage of passing candidates for each filter.

codon_usage_tsv: tsv

A tsv mapping codons to their usage frequency for the organism used.

Returns¶

Generator of all the possible candidate sequence/Renzyme combinations that passed all of the single Renzyme filters. A candidate sequence is very similar to the endogenous sequence, but it has the amino acid change (could be any codon that corresponds to that amino acid) and anywhere from one to the maximum possible number of synonymous substitutions. If ‘get_filter_stats’, it will also write out a file called ‘[locusname]_filter_stats.tsv’ that includes a percentage of candidates that passed for each filter, along with the total number of candidates.

no_endogenous_cutsites_within_Nnt_of_primers(Renzyme, N=5)[source]¶

Filters out Renzymes for all candidates that have endogenous sites within N nucleotides of the primers.

Parameters¶

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction enzyme object

N: int

The desired minimum distance in nucleotides an endogenous site must be from the primers for the Renzyme to pass this filter. Default = 5

Returns¶

False if Renzyme has an endogenous site within Nnt of one of the primers, True otherwise. This function will be easier to write when we’ve fleshed out exactly what sequences we are giving to Endogenous and Candidate

does_not_exceed_max_cutsites(Renzyme, N)[source]¶

Filters out this Renzyme for all candidates it it has more than N cutsites in the endogenous sequence.

Parameters¶

N: int

The maximum number of endogenous cutsites Renzyme is allowed to have.

Returns¶

False if Renzyme has more than N cutsites in the endogenous sequence, True otherwise.

class tiarsdesigner.Candidate(endogenous, sequence)[source]¶

Bases: Designer

The parent class for Endogenous and Candidate, which stores functions and variables common to both

The Candidate class is a subclass of the designer class, and a candidate is a candidate repair oligo with synonymous substitutions to the endogenous sequence within 15 nt of the Cas9 cutsite.

Parameters¶

endogenous: Endogenou object

An Endogenous object, the wildtype sequence that the candidate is based on.

sequence: string

The candidate sequence, very similar to the endogenous object sequence but it has the desired CRISPR/cas9 nonsynonymous substitution, as well as a series of synonymous substitutions within the cutsite region.

Attributes¶

From Parent Class:

sequence cutsite cutsite_region cutsite_frame Renzymes splicing_hexamers

Unique to Candidate Class:

endogenous: Endogenous object

An Endogenous object, the wildtype sequence that the Candidate is based on.

sub_dep_Renzymes: dict

substitution dependent restriction enzymes, a dictionary of Restriction enzymes with cutsites that depend on synonymous substitutions in cutsite_region. This means that the bp substitutions in the Candidate sequence created recognition sites in the candidate sequence for these enzymes that aren’t in the endogenous sequence. In other words, this is a dictionary of enzymes with recognition sites that are in the Candidate sequence but not in the endogenous sequence. If an enzyme has recognition sites in the endogenous sequence AND new additional substitution dependent sites in the candidate sequence, only the novel substitution dependent cutsites will be listed for that enzyme in this dictionary.

sub_dep_Renzyme_recognition_sites: dict

very similar to sub_dep_Renzymes, but the dictionary values are the coordinates of the enzyme recognition sites rather than the cutsites.

num_subs: int

the number of bp substitutions the candidate has compared to the wildtypes sequence (endogenous.sequence)

endogenous_matches: dict

a dictionary of the restriction enzymes with values describing the “polarity” of the endogenous site(s) compared to the substitution dependent site(s). This dictionary will assign ‘None’ restriction enzymes that have sandwiched endogenous or candidate sites (see method ‘no_sandwhiched_cutsites’ for more details. For polarity, ‘0’ means that the restriction enzyme has no endogenous cutsites. A ‘+’ value means that the restriction enzyme has one or more endogenous sites after the substitution dependent cutsite(s) in the sequence string (and none before it). A ‘-’ value means that it has one or more endogenous cutsites before the substitution dependent cutsite(s) in the string (and none after it)

get_hamming_distance()[source]¶

Returns the hamming distance between the endogenous sequence and the candidate sequence, AKA the number of single character substitutions in the candidate (self.sequence) compared to the endogenous sequence (self.endogenous.sequence)

Returns¶

Integer indicating the number of substitutions to the endogenous sequence are in the candidate sequence.

get_substitution_dependent_Renzymes()[source]¶

Finds restriction enzyme cutsites that depend on synonymous substitutions in the cutsite region (AKA they are in the candidate sequence but not the endogenous sequence because one or more substitutions created their recognition site) and returns a dictionary mapping those cutsites to their enzymes.

Returns¶

A dictionary with enzyme names as keys and their substitution dependent cutsites as values. If an enzyme has multiple cutsites in the sequence, it will only return the cutsites that are unique to the candidate sequence (compared to the endogenous self.endogenous.sequence)

get_endogenous_matches()[source]¶

This function will look at restriction enzymes with endogenous and substitution dependent sites, and it’ll return a dictionary of the restriction enzymes with values describing the “polarity” of the endogenous site(s) compared to the substitution dependent site(s).

Returns¶

A dictionary with enzymes as keys and symbols indicating the polarity of their cutsites as values. A ‘0’ value means that the restriction enzyme has no endogenous cutsites. A ‘+’ value means that the restriction enzyme has one or more endogenous sites after the substitution dependent cutsite(s) in the sequence string (and none before it). A ‘-’ value means that it has one or more endogenous cutsites before the substitution dependent cutsite(s) in the string (and none after it). A value of None means that that enzyme either has novel site(s) sandwiched between endogenous sites, or endogenous site(s) sandwiched between novel sites.

get_sub_dep_Renzyme_recognition_sites()[source]¶

Finds restriction enzyme recognition sites within the candidate seq that depend on synonymous substitutions in the cutsite region (AKA they are in the candidate sequence but not the endogenous sequence because one or more substitutions created them) and returns a dictionary mapping those recognition site coordinates to their enzymes.

Returns¶

A dictionary with enzyme names as keys and their substitution dependent recognition site coordinates as values. If an enzyme has multiple recognition sites in the sequence, it will only return the recognition site coordinates that are unique to the candidate sequence (compared to the endogenous self.endogenous.sequence)

get_average_distance_between_RE_cutsites_and_Cas9_cutsite(Renzyme)[source]¶

Returns¶

The average distance in nucleotides between novel cutsite and cas9 cutsite for each novel cutsite for Renzyme in the candidate sequence.

no_new_cutsites()[source]¶

Filters out candidates for which the synonymous changes did not create any new enzyme recognition sites.

Filters out candidates for which the substitutions interferred with splicing hexamers.

Returns¶

False if there are any differences between self.splicing_hexamers and self.endogenous.splicing_hexamers (which would indicate that the candidate’s synonymous changes interfered with the splicing hexamers), True otherwise.

Filters out candidates for which the PAM site could be interrupted by a synonymous change or the desired AA change, but isn’t.

Returns¶

False if the PAM site can be interrupted but isn’t, True otherwise.

False if the Renzyme has any sandwiched cutsites, True otherwise

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

False if Renzyme has an unknown/ambiguous cutsite, True otherwise.

no_endogenous_cutsites_within_Nnt_of_novel_cutsite(Renzyme, N=5)[source]¶

Filters out Renzymes for this candidate that have endogenous cutsites within N nucleotides of a substitution dependent cutsite.

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

The minimum distance in nucleotides any endogenous site can be from any substitution dependent site.

no_lost_endogenous_sites(Renzyme)[source]¶

Filters out Renzymes for this candidate that have endogenous sites that have been interrupted by substitutions, such that they only appear in the endogenous sequence and not in the candidate sequence.

Parameters¶

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False if any endogenous cutsites for Renzyme are lost with the synonymous substitutions, True otherwise

novel_site_depends_on_at_least_two_substitutions(Renzyme)[source]¶

Filters out Renzymes for this candidate that have substitution dependent recognition sites in the candidate sequence that depend on less than two substitutions.

Parameters¶

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False if any of the substitution dependent recognition sites for this Renzyme in this candidate depend on less than two substitutions, True otherwise.

num_recognition_sites_equals_num_cutsites(Renzyme)[source]¶

Filters out any Renzymes for this candidate for which the number of recognition sites in the whole sequence does not equal the number of cutsites for the whole sequence.

Parameters¶

Renzyme: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False if there are a different number of cutsites from recognition sites for Renzyme (which could mean that the enzyme cuts outsite the recognitition site and the Renzyme is close enough to the edge that the cut would not appear in the sequence, or maybe the enzyme cuts twice), True otherwise

at_least_one_has_endogenous_site(RenzymeA, RenzymeB)[source]¶

Filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidate for which neither Renzyme in the pair has an endogenous site.

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False if neither RenzymeA nor RenzymeB have any endogenous sites (AKA if both have polarities of ‘0’), True otherwise.

both_have_endogenous_sites(RenzymeA, RenzymeB)[source]¶

A harsher version of ‘at_least_one_has_endogenous_site’, this filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidate for which at least one of the candidates in the pair does not have an endogenous site.

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False unless both Renzymes have an endogenous site

compatible_polarity(RenzymeA, RenzymeB)[source]¶

Filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidates if they have endogenous sites on opposite sides of their novel sites with respect to the beginning of the sequence (AKA one of the primers).

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

This function will return False if Renzyme A and Renzyme B have incompatible polarities (e.g. if one has a ‘-’ polarity and the other has a ‘+’ polarity), True otherwise.

different_recognition_sites(RenzymeA, RenzymeB)[source]¶

Filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidate that have the same recognition site.

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

False if RenzymeA and RenzymeB have the same recognition site

both_Renzymes_depend_on_at_least_one_unique_substitution(RenzymeA, RenzymeB)[source]¶

Filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidate for which both Renzymes depend on the exact same set of substitutions for their substitution dependent recognition sites.

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

Returns¶

True only if RenzymeA and RenzymeB each depend on at least one substitution that the other does not depend on, False otherwise.

no_unneeded_substitutions(RenzymeA, RenzymeB=None)[source]¶

Filters out Renzyme pairs for this candidate if there are any synonymous substitutions that are not needed to create the novel sites for Renzyme A and B and the desired AA change. If the PAM site cannot be changed, it will not exclude candidates with unneeded substitutions that are within the gRNA target region as long as they have no unneeded substitutions outside the gRNA target region.”

Parameters¶

RenzymeA: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme in the form of a Bio.Restriction object.

RenzymeB: Bio.Restriction enzyme object

A restriction enzyme other than RenzymeA, in the form of a Bio.Restriction object. To run this filter only on RenzymeA, do not specify a RenzymeB

Returns¶

False if there are any unneeded substitutions (unless the PAM can’t be changed, in which case there can be unneeded substitutions as long as they are within the gRNA target region), True otherwise.
